- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is below recent highs, model tends to underreact — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, model overestimates bullish momentum — reduce forecast by 1–2% per low sentiment day.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon when sentiment is rising — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.5 over last 5 days.
- If forecast is below 65.00 and sentiment is rising, model is too pessimistic — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment rises sharply, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days unless price is already trending.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- If forecast is above 68.00 and sentiment is falling, model overreacts — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment <0.4 for 3+ days.
- Forecast often misses 30-day trend if sentiment is low — if sentiment <0.3 for 5+ days, forecast should be 1–2% below recent 18-day average.
